The Japanese Kikkō 亀甲 (tortoise shell) pattern is made of interlocking hexagons, echoing the shell of a tortoise. In Japan the tortoise is a symbol of longevity, endurance, and good fortune, so this motif has long been used to wish someone a long, healthy life. Its tightly packed, unbroken hexagons also read as a sign of protection and stability, which is why the pattern shows up on kimono, armor, and family crests alike.
